To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diversity of secondary woody plants in thermophilous oak-dominated forests in central Italy is high and each of the species has a unique set of traits that contribute to important ecosystem functions and socio-economically relevant services, but the diversity and composition of these species is not associated with the diversity of dominant trees.

1) the diversity of secondary woody plants in thermophilous forests of central Italy is high, with 40 species in three functional groups; 2) the composition of the AWS community is not affected by the richness of dominant tree species, but the diversity of AWS shrubs is related to the cover of the dominant tree layer; 3) each AWS possesses, on average, five functional traits over a total 13 that contribute to important ecosystem functions and socio-economically important benefits
the diversity of secondary woody plants (sporadic trees, shrub and vines) in thermophilous forests is high and is related to the species richness of dominant tree species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of secondary woody plants in the understory of thermophilous forests and the potential role of this group of plants as providers of ecosystem functions and socio‐economic benefits.
the diversity of secondary woody taxa in thermophilous forests of central Italy, and the relationships between this diversity and the species richness of dominant woody species.
the diversity of secondary woody plants in relation to species diversity and cover of dominant species in thermophilous forest ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although AWS are not a key factor in determining the structure and functioning of the thermophilous decideous forests, they are an essential component of these forests, contributing to their biodiversity and multifunctionality.
AWS diversity and composition is mainly determined by site factors rather than by the dominant tree community.
the diversity of the AWS is not affected by the diversity of the dominant tree species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AWS are a key feature of thermophilous forests in central Italy and that their diversity and contribution to ecosystem functions are not affected by the richness of the dominant trees, which is the main determinant of forest diversity in this ecosystem type.
, in these forests, AWS species richness is high and their composition is stable, while their contribution to ecosystem functions is high and variable.
AWS are an integral part of the forest ecosystems and should not be considered as mere “by-catch”.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diversity of AWS is high in these forests and is related to that of the dominant tree species, suggesting that the conservation of both is essential to preserve the multifunctionality of these ecosystems.
, although AWS are not the most abundant components of thermophilous forests, they are a highly diverse and functionally important component of these ecosystems.
AWS are an important component of thermophilous forests that should not be neglected when planning forest management strategies.
